newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GARPENLOV SCORES TWICE IN THIRD AS DEVILS, PANTHERS TIE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GARPENLOV SCORES TWICE IN THIRD AS DEVILS, PANTHERS TIE.

text.p: The tie was no surprise, but Johan Garpenlov made it dramatic.

Garpenlov scored twice in a 3:40 span of the third period to rally the Florida Panthers into a 2-2 tie with the New Jersey Devils Friday in a battle of the NHL's top two defensive teams, who have recorded a combined total of seven ties in their last eight games.
The Devils carried a 1-0 edge into the third period on Bobby Holik's first-period goal and doubled their lead on Bill Guerin's goal at 1:03.
But Garpenlov tipped Terry Carkner's wrist shot from the top of the left faceoff circle past goaltender Martin Brodeur at 3:53. The goal ended Florida's scoreless streak at 118 minutes, 10 seconds.

Goalie John Vanbiesbrouck kept the Panthers in the game when he stopped Guerin on a breakaway seconds later and Florida capitalised at 7:33 when Garpenlov's slap shot from the top of the left circle beat Brodeur to the stick side.
The puck may have deflected off the stick of New Jersey defenceman Shawn Chambers, but not even he knew for sure.

"I asked the same thing," Chambers said. "I didn't feel it touch my stick, but Marty (Brodeur) said it did move a little bit. It could have just touched it or it could have just knuckled on him. It's a tough goal for us to take there."
"Mellanby made a good pass. I was lucky because the puck was bouncing and I shot it and got it through on the short side," Garpenlov said.

Vanbiesbrouck came up big again with 16.8 seconds to go in overtime when he used his glove to snare a short wrist shot by Steve Sullivan, who snuck behind the Panthers' defence on a pass by Bobby Holik.

"Sullivan is a little scooter and I knew I just had to hold my ground and make the save," Vanbiesbrouck said. "It was a very well-played game. It was exciting and one of the better Devil-Panthers games. We persevered, got the good bounces and escaped with the point."

Rob Niedermayer, whose brother Scott plays for the Devils, assisted on both goals for Florida, which has played to three straight ties and is winless in its last four (0-3-1). The Panthers have won just once in their last seven road games and are 0-9-4 when trailing after two periods.

"It was a defensive battle, but both goaltenders had to make big saves at key times," Florida coach Doug MacLean said. "Vanbiesbrouck made a huge save in overtime on the kid Sullivan and our penalty-killing came through huge for us at a key time."
New Jersey is 4-2-6 in its last 12 games.
Florida has allowed an NHL-low 123 goals, while the Devils are second with 124 goals-against.
Vanbiesbrouck finished with 33 saves, while Brodeur stopped 27 shots.
In Calgary, rookie Jarome Iginla set up three goals and Trevor Kidd made 25 saves, leading the Flames to a 5-2 victory over the sputtering Washington Capitals.

Calgary jumped to a 3-0 lead early in the second period and held on to escape the Pacific Division basement. The Flames have won six of their last nine home games and moved into a tie with Anaheim, two points behind Chicago for the final Western Conference playoff spot.
Robert Reichel and German Titov scored first-period goals and Ed Ward tallied in the second against shaky goaltender Jim Carey, who was replaced by Olaf Kolzig.
Dave Gagner and Todd Hlushko tallied for Calgary in the third period.
Jaroslav Sjevkovsky and Joe Reekie had the goals for Washington, which is winless in six of its last seven games and fell to 1-1-1 on its five-game road trip.
